We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. 【文章原文节选】: HackerTube – karpathy karpathy Home Blog HackerTube 31 Oct, 2026 It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org ! Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews , filtered them, ran Sonnet over them in a Workflow (Claude Code feature), got rid of spam, and narrowed everything down to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics. Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila! Four years ago, I wrote this blog post describing what I had in the 40-liter backpack that I travel around with. Physical minimalism, however, was an idea that came of age in the 2000s and 2010s and was responding to the challenges and the opportunities of the 2000s and 2010s. Mukul Goyal Oct 28, 2026 12 mins October 26, 2026 Fixed P1 Severity In October 2026, we found a way to turn an ordinary public ChatGPT share into attacker-controlled JavaScript running inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it. 【文章原文节选】: Jepsen: ParticleDB 1.1.4 JEPSEN Blog Analyses Talks Consistency Services Ethics ParticleDB 1.1.4 Kyle Kingsbury 2026-10-31 ParticleDB is a multi-model database designed for AI workloads. We tested versions 1.1.4 through 1.1.18.11.rc-22 and found that ParticleDB’s claims of “Full ACID” were somewhat premature. We present 96 issues in ParticleDB, ranging from the pedestrian (crashes, deadlocks, data loss, etc.) to the piquant (partially-invisible rows which could not be deleted, WHERE 4 = 5 , dropped tables re-emerging in distorted forms, confused columns, strings turning into integers, and so on). Most issues required just a single server, single client, and no faults. By version 1.1.18.11.rc-22, all but ten of those issues appeared resolved. However, ParticleDB continued to lose committed writes during normal operation with the default occ transaction mode, and allowed internal anomalies and Lost Update with serializable , the strongest setting. Orkes, the makers of ParticleDB, have since released version 1.1.19-rc.13; they claim that it resolves all remaining issues discussed in this report.
